Thanks — quick summary from security team: 

1) Pen test report: we can provide a redacted pen test report. Redaction rules: remove attacker IPs, internal-only configs, and any third-party creds. We will keep full technical details for internal review. Recommend delivering via secure Drive link with access audited.

2) Remediation SLA: our public stance is: Critical severity: 7 days to mitigate or implement compensating control; High: 30 days; Medium: 90 days; Low: tracked per sprint. We can represent these as expected time-to-remediate windows; for enterprise customers we offer runbook cadence and quarterly risk reviews.

3) Scanning cadence: we run authenticated vulnerability scans weekly on infra and daily unauthenticated smoke checks for exposed endpoints; full external pentest exercises semi-annually or after major rewrites. We include results in our internal tracker and maintain a rolling 12-month evidence archive.

4) Vulnerability disclosure: we have a coordinated disclosure policy and a security@redwood.ai inbox for reports; triage within 48 hours, triage lead assigns owner, and public disclosure only after mitigations or compensating controls. We will attach a one-page summary for Finova.

Attachments: [redwood-scan-policy-2026.md] 

I propose we: (a) draft a permitted-use template (legal to sign) allowing us to share redacted artifacts; (b) prepare an executive summary of pen-test findings; (c) provide the redacted report and the SLA language. Sergio
